mcp.note: ADDED 2026-08-23. This block did not exist, and its absence read to mcp-maintain's preflight exactly like enabled:false — a skip, reported green, about a surface that has been serving in production. FuzeInfra runs the handoff MCP server: agent-templates/orchestration/handoff_mcp/server.py (FastMCP, 7 @mcp.tool functions: spawn_agent, resume_session, ask_agent, approve, memory_write, memory_read, reach_human), built as ghcr.io/izzywdev/fuzeinfra/agent-handoff and deployed by helm/fuzeinfra/templates/handoff-mcp.yaml as the `handoff-mcp` Deployment + Service (:8000) + Ingress on mcp-handoff.<domain>. helm/fuzeinfra/values-contabo.yaml sets handoffMcp.enabled:true, and the pod was observed Running in production on 2026-08-21 (cluster-query run 32475207623). NOT THE GATEWAY DIALECT, and deliberately so: this is NOT the shared OpenAPI->MCP gateway. It is FuzeInfra's own hand-written server with its own image, it projects no OpenAPI document, and there is no contracts/openapi.yaml in this repo for a gateway to project — so it carries `entry` (the server code) plus `image`/`deployment`/`endpoints`, and no `spec`/`overrides`/`implementation`. Transport is streamable-HTTP (server.py builds mcp.streamable_http_app() behind uvicorn and a HANDOFF_MCP_TOKEN bearer middleware), NOT stdio: the module docstring's `python server.py` line is the same process, served over HTTP. `enabled:true` MIRRORS THE HELM GATE — IT IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE SERVICE WORKS. values-contabo.yaml itself spells out that it does not, end to end: helm/fuzeinfra/files/handoff-state/*.json are still `{}` placeholders because the Provision Managed Agents workflow fails on Anthropic credit (run 32322608863), so the server starts, serves, and fails every tool call with "unknown role"; and the Cloudflare Access bypass in front of mcp-handoff.prod.fuzefront.com may still 302 machine callers into an email-OTP login. A surface that is real, reachable and broken is precisely what this manifest must stop hiding. WHAT THIS ACTUALLY CHANGES DOWNSTREAM — stated from the workflows as they exist today, and NOT from the assumption that adding this block turns a check red. IT DOES NOT, and the reason is worse than that: THIS REPO HAS NO .github/workflows/mcp-maintain.yml AT ALL. Every other product repo in the fleet is stamped with one; FuzeInfra is not — verified by listing .github/workflows/ on main. So the MCP surface FuzeInfra actually runs in production has never been assessed by anything, and adding this block does not by itself change that. (For reference, the sibling a2a-maintain.yml here is the newer LiteLLM-gateway generation and its own comment states the policy explicitly: 'Any failure is a SKIP, not a red.') THE VACUOUS GATE HERE IS THIS FILE PLUS A MISSING WORKFLOW, NOT A FAILING ONE. Nothing in CI cross-checks the manifest against the chart's effective prod values either. Two follow-ups, neither in this change: stamp mcp-maintain.yml into this repo, and add a gate that diffs manifest surface flags against the chart. `toolCount`/`irreversibleTools` are not declared because nothing here enumerated the surface from a running server; mcp-maintainer fills them in from a real run. Note that spawn_agent, reach_human and memory_write are all externally-visible or irreversible on their face and will need explicit classification.

a2a.note: Policy REVERSED 2026-09-04 -- FuzeInfra will host a genuine PRODUCT tenant (infra-platform: role.json + .claude/skills/fuzeinfra-platform-expert landed) in addition to the four Exec-* tenants; servingRoles already names it and tests/test_a2a_surface.py already enforces the new shape. Left enabled:false because gate-a2a I0 correctly flags that no chart values file yet carries an a2a: block for this tenant -- flipping enabled:true first would advertise a card routing to a pod that does not exist. Next PR: the Helm a2a block for infra-platform (devops-engineer), matching the pattern already used by other product repos, then flip this to true.

clusterOps.note: FuzeInfra OWNS the cluster, so it is the one repo whose `@fuze` entrypoint may hold prod credentials. This flag installs workflow-templates/fuze-cluster.yml (kubectl/helm/terraform + the prod kubeconfig secret + the in-cluster arc-runners pool). It is HALF the gate: the workflow is inert until repo variable FUZE_CLUSTER_ENTRYPOINT=true is set by a human, so no automated propagation path can switch on prod cluster access by itself. CLAUDE.baseline.md 1 forbids any consuming repo from declaring this — a product repo carrying clusterOps is a governance finding, not a feature.
